sentences.text: Antarctopelta was a stocky, herbivorous quadruped protected by skin-embedded armor plates, sharing these defensive traits with other ankylosaurians.
This medium-sized ankylosaur reached at least 4 meters in length and remains the only known ankylosaur from Antarctica.
The holotype specimen MLP 86-X-28-1 is the sole known material of the genus, consisting of approximately 15% of the skeleton, including skull fragments, vertebrae, limb bones, and armor pieces.
Its tail likely ended in a macuahuitl, a cluster of spiked osteoderms resembling an Aztec weapon, a structure similar to that of its relative Stegouros.
A 2019 histological analysis revealed that the individual represented by the holotype was sexually mature.
Bone growth rates in Antarctopelta remained consistent despite different climatic conditions compared to lower latitude ankylosaurs.
The only known specimen was discovered in January 1986 by Argentine geologists Eduardo Olivero and Robert Scasso on James Ross Island in the Antarctic Peninsula.
It was the second dinosaur formally named from Antarctica, following Cryolophosaurus in 1994.
The genus and type species Antarctopelta oliveroi were formally described in 2006 by Leonardo Salgado and Zulma Gasparini.
The discovery of a shark tooth and bivalves with the specimen suggests Antarctopelta died and floated out to sea, a behavior seen in other ankylosaurs.
Despite being preserved in a marine environment, Antarctopelta is similar to other ankylosaurians that lived on land.
It possibly coexisted with the ornithopod Trinisaura.
The genus belongs to the subfamily Parankylosauria, a group that includes Stegouros.
A 2011 phylogenetic analysis suggested that Antarctopelta is the most basal known nodosaurid, though this placement has been debated.
It shares traits with both ankylosaurids and nodosaurids, making family assignment difficult so it has been designated as Ankylosauria incertae sedis.
During Antarctopelta's time, Earth was warmer and humider, leaving Antarctica ice-free.
The holotype skeleton was found about 90 meters from the base of the Gamma Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation.
